topics.title: Hardy–Weinberg
topics.teacherTextbookAssignment: 680–682 #1–5; 683 Practice Problems 1–5; 684–685 #6,7; 688 #1–8  (you may finish these the next day as it is a shorter lesson)

parts.title: Populations and allele counts
parts.operation: Convert genotype counts into allele counts with the two-copy denominator

parts.title: Allele and genotype frequencies
parts.operation: Calculate and distinguish observed allele frequencies and expected genotype frequencies

parts.title: Equilibrium assumptions
parts.operation: Explain each assumption and identify which information a case does not supply

parts.title: Solving and checking
parts.operation: Solve a population problem and check both equations and predicted counts

parts.title: A model and its limits
parts.operation: Compare data with expectations without assuming phenotype frequencies reveal all genotypes

parts.title: Mutation and selection
parts.operation: Explain allele origin separately from changes in representation

parts.title: Chance and population size
parts.operation: Compare random sampling effects and distinguish founder from bottleneck events

parts.title: Movement and mating
parts.operation: Distinguish changes in allele frequencies from genotype-frequency changes alone

parts.title: Resistance and evidence
parts.operation: Explain change across generations without claiming organisms mutate because they need to

parts.title: Testing explanations
parts.operation: Compare supplied population data and revise a mechanism claim
requiredSkillOperations: formulate question and plan a controlled comparison
record supplied observations and data with units
calculate or compare evidence and test an explanation
communicate a reasoned claim, consider a supplied alternative and revise
parts.scopeLimit: Independent digital work demonstrates these operations; teamwork and physical laboratory performance require separate teacher observation.

parts.title: Size and density
parts.operation: Calculate density with units and distinguish it from total size

parts.title: Sampling populations
parts.operation: Estimate population size from supplied counts and explain sampling assumptions
requiredSkillOperations: formulate question and plan a controlled comparison
record supplied observations and data with units
calculate or compare evidence and test an explanation
communicate a reasoned claim, consider a supplied alternative and revise
parts.scopeLimit: Independent digital work demonstrates these operations; teamwork and physical laboratory performance require separate teacher observation.

parts.title: Four demographic processes
parts.operation: Calculate net change from all four counts

parts.title: Rates and denominators
parts.operation: Calculate rates with explicit interval and denominator

parts.title: Exponential and logistic models
parts.operation: Construct and compare growth curves using supplied data

parts.title: Feedback and changing limits
parts.operation: Interpret deviations from a model without treating carrying capacity as fixed forever

parts.title: Life-history strategies
parts.operation: Compare trait continua and qualify idealized r/K categories

parts.title: Interactions and their effects
parts.operation: Classify relationships by effects and justify classifications with evidence

parts.title: Competition and defence
parts.operation: Explain how a mechanism changes survival or access to resources

parts.title: Population cycles
parts.operation: Interpret paired abundance curves and compare alternative causes

parts.title: Succession and disturbance
parts.operation: Compare starting conditions and explain non-universal community pathways

parts.title: Ecological decisions and communication
parts.operation: Evaluate a supplied conservation investigation and communicate a qualified recommendation
